issues.description: The template repository does not contain the server/client Spring Boot project or any of the classes/types referenced in the problem statement (e.g. PersonResource, PersonService, PersonController, Common.Person, REST endpoints). Instead the template only includes unrelated sorting example classes (BubbleSort, MergeSort, Client). This structural mismatch prevents students from following the exercise: required packages, classes, and REST scaffolding referenced throughout the problem are missing, so students cannot implement or run the described tasks.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a template repository that matches the problem statement: include the server-side Spring Boot skeleton (packages and classes such as PersonResource, PersonService, PersonSortingOptions, domain model Common.Person, NoteResource example) and the client-side controller stubs (PersonController using WebClient). Alternatively, adjust the problem statement to describe the sorting exercise present in the template. Ensure the template contains the expected package structure and placeholder methods/classes for the REST endpoints so students can implement the tasks.

issues.description: The problem statement describes a REST application with server and client classes such as PersonResource, PersonService, PersonController, NoteResource and H05E01ServerApplication, but the provided template repository contains an unrelated sorting example (Client, BubbleSort, MergeSort). This mismatch means the same conceptual entities referenced in the exercise instructions (persons/notes and REST controllers/services) are not present in the template under the expected identifiers, preventing students from mapping requirements to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template repository with the problem statement by providing the expected REST skeleton and identifiers: add placeholder classes/files using the names from the specification (e.g. PersonResource, PersonService, PersonController, NoteResource, H05E01ServerApplication, Starter). Alternatively, if the sorting example is intentional, update the problem statement to reference the sorting classes (Client, BubbleSort, MergeSort) to keep names consistent across artifacts.
